title: Spot a fake text from your bank

cards.text: The FTC says people may pretend to be your bank and text about a suspicious charge. An unexpected message can be a trick.
cards.line: A familiar name does not prove the message is real.

cards.text: The FTC says not to click a link in an unexpected message. Open your bank's official app or website yourself instead.
If you are worried, the FTC says to call the number on your statement. Do not use a number in the text.
cards.line: Use a number you already trust.

checks.prompt: A text says your bank saw a problem and gives a link. What is safer?
checks.why: The FTC says not to click links in unexpected messages. Contact the company through an official app or website.

checks.prompt: You want to call your bank about a worrying text. Which number should you use?
options: A number the sender gives you
checks.why: The FTC says to use a number you find on your statement, not the number in the message.

checks.prompt: A text asks for your account details. What should you do?
options: Share them if the logo looks right
checks.why: The FTC says real companies will not ask for account information by text.

takeaway: Ignore the link and contact your bank through a number or app you trust.
